pressure_signals.description: FY2026 EDINET record reports totalShareholderReturn=1.004 versus totalReturnSharePriceIndex=2.022. This is used only as a relative-dislocation signal; it is not treated as a current-price return calculation.

Large-shareholding events show Asset Management One declining from 5.04% to 3.98% by 2026-04-30 and then to 2.13% by 2026-07-15. A separate pure-investment filer, Sumitomo Mitsui DS Asset Management, declined from 3.92% to 3.36% by 2026-04-30. These are observed seller-flow signals, not evidence of forced liquidation.

reasons: FY2026 operating cash flow increased 21.18% year-on-year.
Two independent observable pressure signals are present: relative TSR underperformance and dated large-holder reductions.
The 2026 event capture through 2026-08-13 contains earnings summaries and a dividend increase, but no negative earnings-revision event.
The evidence supports observable seller-flow/dislocation only; forced liquidation or causal sufficiency is not claimed.
FY2026 filing-date PER is 10.0x, at the pre-registered threshold.
FY2026 filing-date FCF yield is approximately 10.18%.
FY2026 filing-date net cash / market cap ratio is approximately 0.54.

limitations: PER, PBR, FCF yield and net-cash ratio here use the filing-date market price embedded in the EDINET DB annual record, not a live 2026-08-13 market quote.
The shareholder reductions establish observed supply from named holders but do not prove forced selling, margin calls or that those sales caused the stock-price path.
The TSR fields are disclosure-record total-return measures and are used as a relative-dislocation feature, not as a precise event-window drawdown.
This artifact ranks research priority only. A fresh point-in-time Decision Snapshot is still required before any human investment decision.
